sentences.text: Revenue grew from $23.7 billion in FY2016 to $51.8 billion in FY2025, a 9.1% CAGR [F1][F10][F168].
Every table revenue figure is a later recast, below the first-reported $58.9 billion for FY2025, so growth and margins mix two presentations [F10][X10].
The cycle was sharpest earlier: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 and rose 153.2% in FY2021 [D161][D200], and the cited filings do not explain those years.
Revenue rose 76.5% to $61.0 billion in FY2022 on higher realized commodity prices and volumes from the Shell Permian acquisition [F7][D238][P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [F8][D274][P47].
Revenue rose 4.9% in FY2025, and Lower 48 contributed 8.0pp of that growth while making up 70.2% of revenue [D342][D713][D711].
Alaska subtracted 1.7pp as its revenue fell 14.0% [D754][D753].
The filing attributes the FY2025 increase to higher volumes, including Marathon Oil, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices [P28][D342].
Net income fell 13.6% while revenue grew 4.9%, so profit lagged revenue in FY2025 [D343][D342].
Diluted share count rose 6.1%, so EPS fell 18.7%, faster than the 13.6% decline in net income [D356][D344][D343].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the window median of 17.9% and far below the 30.6% high [F30][D831][D830].
Cost of revenue rose to 37.9% of revenue from 36.6%, and D&A rose to 19.5% from 17.5% [D326][D292][D330][D296].
The filing says DD&A increased $1,901 million in 2025, mainly from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22][D330].
SG&A fell to 1.5% of revenue from 2.1% because 2024 included $545 million of Marathon Oil transaction expenses [P23][D328][D294].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4%, and the cited filings do not explain that move [D332][D298].
Operating cash flow was $19.8 billion in FY2025, 2.48x net income, versus 1.54x in FY2019 [F59][D333][D109].
Operating cash flow slipped from $20.1 billion in 2024 because of lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6][F58].
The table has no capex or free cash flow after FY2022, but the filing cites $12.6 billion of capital spending and investments in 2025 against D&A of $11.5 billion [P7][X61].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion in FY2025, up 13.4%, and the current ratio was 1.30x against a window median of 1.45x [D335][D357][F153][D843].
Reported total debt of $1.0 billion equals only the current portion, so net cash of $7.1 billion and its 100th percentile among six peers are unreliable [D336][X203][D337][D850].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $9.0 billion in FY2025, 46% of operating cash flow, with $0.9 billion also used to retire debt [D339][P31][P7].
Diluted share count still rose 6.1% despite $5.0 billion of buybacks, and the cited filings do not explain the increase [D356][X141].
Data quality (R1, high): table revenue is recast for all ten years versus the first-reported figures, so cross-year growth and margins are not like for like [R1][F10][X10].
In FY2025 total debt shows only a $1.0 billion current portion, while interest expense rose to $1.2 billion, which the filing ties to debt assumed from Marathon Oil [D336][X203][X81][P10].
Net income has fallen three years running, from $18.7 billion in FY2022 to $8.0 billion in FY2025, a 24.7% annual decline [F17][F20][D845].
D&A reached 19.5% of revenue in FY2025 against 9.6% in FY2022, driven by the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher volumes [D330][D221][P22].
The FY2023 revenue decline (R2) looks benign: it was price-driven and revenue has since recovered [R2][F8][F10][P47].
Operating cash flow below the FY2025 level of $19.8 billion in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the price-driven slide described in the filing [F59][P6].
Net margin staying below 15.4% in the FY2026 10-K would confirm erosion further from the 17.9% window median; a move above the median would reverse it [F30][D831].
A diluted share count change that turns negative, against the 6.1% increase in FY2025, would show buybacks outpacing issuance in the FY2026 10-K [D356].
